name: Environmental Systems Analysis and Decision Making
description: Introduction to natural and man-made systems. Systems thinking in environmental contexts: Feedback loops, resilience, and tipping points. Global environmental challenges: Climate change, pollution, biodiversity loss, and resource scarcity. Role of systems analysis in informed decision-making for sustainability. Systems modeling applied to environmental systems. Nature of environmental systems, the model building process addressing specific environmental problems. Strategies for analyzing and using environmental systems models. Fate and transport models for contaminants in air, water, and soil. Optimization methods (search techniques, linear programming, non-linear programming, dynamic programming) to evaluate alternatives for solid-waste management and water and air pollution control. Sequential decision-making for long-term environmental strategies. Time-dependent analysis: Discounting environmental benefits, lifecycle impacts, and future uncertainties. Multi-Objective and Multi stakeholder Optimization. Balancing ecological, economic, and social priorities (e.g., cost vs. ecosystem health). Multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA), Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP), and trade-off analysis. Systems design for waste reduction, resource recovery, and closed-loop cycles. Modelling and valuing biodiversity and ecosystem services.
